title: Vatican II and Modern Catholic Renewal
welcome_lead: Step inside Saint Peter's Basilica as bishops gather for the Second Vatican Council, 1962-65.
meta_desc: IBDP Religious Studies Adventure: Vatican II, its key documents and modern Catholic renewal.
final_note: You have witnessed a watershed for Catholicism. Vatican II continues to be interpreted today.

concepts.def: Second Vatican Council (1962-65) convened by Pope John XXIII to renew Catholic life and engagement with the modern world.
Vatican II Dogmatic Constitution on the Church (1964) emphasising the Church as 'People of God'.
Vatican II Constitution on the Sacred Liturgy (1963) allowing vernacular language in worship.
1965 Declaration on the Church's relation with non-Christian religions, transforming Jewish-Catholic relations.
Italian for 'updating', John XXIII's term for the renewal he sought.
Movement promoting Christian unity, expressed in the Decree Unitatis Redintegratio.

walkthroughs.body_html: Pope John XXIII surprised the world by convoking Vatican II in 1959; it opened on 11 October 1962 and ran for four sessions. He spoke of aggiornamento — bringing the Church up to date — and the need for the 'medicine of mercy' rather than condemnation.

Sacrosanctum Concilium permitted vernacular liturgy; Lumen Gentium developed ecclesiology as 'People of God'; Dei Verbum renewed approaches to scripture; Gaudium et Spes articulated the Church's engagement with the joys and sorrows of the modern world.

Interpretation has been contested between 'reform-in-continuity' and 'rupture' readings. Pope Paul VI implemented many changes; John Paul II and Benedict XVI emphasised hermeneutics of continuity; Pope Francis (Jesuit, since 2013) has highlighted pastoral and synodal emphases.
